Entries.Text: Write the {0} ESD files with unsaved changes into the project. A binder keeps its other entries and its compression.
ESD Editor: failed to load the catalogue {0}. Commands and functions show as raw IDs.
ESD Editor: failed to list the ESD files.
ESD Editor: couldn't read the names in {0}; the ESD still shows.
ESD Editor: {0} is no longer in {1}, so the file wasn't saved.
The project's ESD files, by what they script. A binder opens to the ESDs in it.
The project has its own copy of this file.
NPC dialogue, shops, and the menus at NPCs and rest points: one ESD per talk ID.
Character state machines (c0000, enemyCommon, chresdbnd). Names are documented for DS1 / DS1R only; most of their args aren't typed.
Menu scripts (menuesdbnd). No names are documented for these: commands and functions show as raw IDs.
DS2 event scripts (/ezstate/event_*). Names come from the catalogue; most args aren't typed.
DS2 enemy AI scripts (/ezstate/ai*). Names come from the catalogue; most args aren't typed.
ESD files of no known kind.
The ESD's state machines: entry machines first, then sub-machines (x0, x1...), which other machines start with a call.
Open the binder and select one of its ESDs.
Machine {0} ({1}): a sub-machine, started by call blocks in this file.

The selected machine's states as blocks. Click to select, double-click (or Enter) a transition to go to its state or a call to go to its machine, Backspace to go back. Up/Down step through the blocks.
Click a value chip to edit it, or a transition's state chip to change where it goes. Right-click a block to add, duplicate, delete or move; Delete, Ctrl+D and the reorder keys work on the selected block.
State {0}: a transition goes to state {1}, which this machine doesn't have.
State {0}: a call starts machine {1}, which this file doesn't have.
State {0}: {1} is called with {2} args; the catalogue documents {3} to {4} (vanilla has a few of these).
State {0}: bytes that don't decode as an expression.
Select a block in the States window.
Add an empty state (the next free id). Nothing goes to it until a transition does.
ESD Editor: state 0 is where the machine starts, so it can't be deleted.
ESD Editor: {1} transitions still go to state {0}. Point them elsewhere first.
Add a transition that is never taken, to this state: set its test and its target next.
Add a condition tested after this one passes (never taken, to this state, until you set it).
This condition is shared by {0} places: give this place its own copy, so editing it changes only here.
The constant 0: the transition is never taken (a way to switch one off).
Start another machine of this file. Its args are added as none: the called machine reads what it's given.
Not used by any vanilla file of this game.
A whole number (decimal or 0x hex). Enter to set.
This condition is shared: the change applies everywhere it's used. Right-click it > Make Unique to change only this place.
Back to where the last transition or call was followed from (Backspace).
How many call blocks in this file start this machine. Properties lists the machines they're in.
States no transition of this machine leads to (state 0, where the machine starts, isn't counted). Vanilla files have these too.
The catalogue has no names for this game or kind of ESD, so commands and functions show as raw IDs.
{0} on entry, {1} while, {2} on exit commands; {3} transitions.

The machine starts here (state 0: every vanilla machine has one).
{0} on entry, {1} while, {2} on exit commands; {3} transitions.
Always taken (its test is the constant 1).
When the test passes, the machine goes to state {0} (double-click to go there).
When the test passes, the conditions inside are tested next.
This condition is used in {0} places of the machine (states and parent conditions share it).
Starts another machine of this file with these args (double-click to go there). The state usually waits for it with a call status test.
Ends this machine, returning the value to the call that started it.
The catalogue has no entry for this command.
A command outside bank 1 that isn't a call or return; its meaning isn't documented.
Called with {0} args; the catalogue documents {1} to {2}.
Details of the selected block, or of the machine when nothing is selected.
The machines of this file with call blocks starting this one, and how many. Click to go there.
Nothing in this file calls it.
Nothing in this file calls it: the game starts entry machines.
The states with a transition (at any depth) to this one. Click to go there.
Go to the machine this call starts.
These bytes don't decode as one expression.

Code view: the machine as a function. A state only one transition reaches is drawn inside it, so chains read as sequences and branches as if / else if / else. Other states are drawn after the state every path to them passes through.
State view: every state as its own block, in ID order, exactly as the file stores them.
Both views edit the same data.

Transitions the code view can't nest: a jump back to a state that isn't a loop around it (two loops entered from different places), or from an unreached part into the rest. They're drawn as 'go to' with the state chip in orange.

Machine {0}. It reads {1} args (arg0 is the call's first value).
A call block in another machine starts it; a return block ends it.
A transition inside this state's block comes back here (repeat).
None of this state's transitions is 'always': it tests them every frame and stays until one passes ('when').
This state has no transitions: the machine stays here. What's drawn after it doesn't follow from it.

State {0}, drawn here because this is the only transition to it.
{1} on entry, {2} while, {3} on exit commands; {4} transitions.

State {0}, reached by more than one transition (or a loop head): each one jumps here.
{1} on entry, {2} while, {3} on exit commands; {4} transitions.
Passes once the machine this state called has returned (ESDLang's call.Done()). The conditions inside branch on its result.
Goes to state {0}, drawn right after this block.
Goes to state {0}, drawn further down (double-click to go there).
Goes back to state {0}, the loop this block is in (double-click to go there).
Goes to state {0}: a jump the code view can't nest (double-click to go there).

Drag a command onto a block in the States window: before a command, at the end of a state's entry commands, or at the end of a transition's pass commands (double-click inserts after the selected block). Drag a function, operator or value onto a value chip to replace it, or onto a transition to change its test.
Select a state, transition or command to insert after.

On a value chip: the value goes on the left (x), the shown default on the right. On a transition: wraps the whole test. && 1, || 0, + 0, - 0, * 1 and / 1 change nothing until you edit the right side; a comparison starts at 0.
A literal value, to edit after dropping.
One of this machine's args (the value its caller passed).
The result of the machine this state called (ESDLang's call.Get()).
Type the transition's test, e.g. GetEventFlag(1234) == 1 && arg0 > 2. Parts you leave as they were keep their exact bytes.
Type one of the command's args as an expression: a value, arg0, a function call or any calculation.
Test (Enter to apply, Esc to cancel)
Arg (Enter to apply, Esc to cancel)
Functions by name or f<id>; ints, 1.5f floats, 1.5 doubles, "strings"; arg0, r0, (r0 = x), CallStatus, CallDone; + - * / < <= > >= == != op96 && ||.
The string has no closing quote.
Only a number can be negative: ESD has no negation (write 0 - x).
Unknown name: not arg<n>, r<n>, CallStatus, CallDone or a value of this arg's enum.
Unknown function: not in the catalogue (use f<id> for an undocumented one).
More than one function has this name: use f<id>.
A function call takes at most 6 args.

A new empty state right after this one: this state's transitions (and its while and on exit commands) move to the new state, and this state goes to it always. Nothing changes until you add commands to it, or give the new 'go to' a test to make this state wait.
A new transition just before this state's final 'always', to a new empty state that goes on to the same place. Its test is 'never' until you set it, so nothing changes until then.
Needs a state whose last transition is 'always' with a target (a state that decides at once). For a state that waits, add a transition instead.
A new state after this one that calls the machine (0 for each arg it reads) and waits until it's done; this state's transitions move inside its 'when call done' block.
Deletes this state (with its commands) and reconnects: every transition to it goes where it went instead.
Only a state with one transition, 'always', to another state, holding nothing, can be taken out of the flow.
A new sub-machine (the next x<n>): state 0 goes to state 1, which returns 0. Call it from another machine with a call block.
A copy of this machine with a new ID: the next sub-machine for a sub-machine, the next entry ID for an entry machine. Calls still go to the original.
An entry machine: the game may start it by its ID, even though no call in the file does.
Another machine of the file calls this one. Remove those calls first (Properties lists the callers).
An ESD needs at least one machine.
No free sub-machine ID is left.
When the test passes, the machine goes to state {0}, drawn inside this block.
